question: How much money was allotted by the Gujarat government in August 2023 for the One District, One Product (ODOP) Programme to promote its indigenous products at the international level?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ₹58 crore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In August 2023, the Gujarat government allotted about ₹58 crore for the "One District, One Product (ODOP)" programme to promote its indigenous/local products at the international level. (ओडीओपी — गुजरात, ₹58 करोड़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The ODOP initiative aims to identify and promote one distinctive product from each district, boosting local manufacturing, employment and exports.

• It aligns with the "Vocal for Local" and "Atmanirbhar Bharat" vision.

NOTE

• ODOP is often linked with GI (Geographical Indication) tags. Examples: Bhagalpur silk (Bihar), Firozabad glassware (UP), Kanchipuram silk (Tamil Nadu).

question: In the context of microfinance in India, the concept of SHG-BLP is used. What does L stand for in SHG-BLP?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Linkage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In microfinance, "SHG-BLP" stands for the "Self Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme". Here, "L" stands for "Linkage". (एसएचजी-बैंक लिंकेज कार्यक्रम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme was launched by NABARD in 1992 to connect Self Help Groups (SHGs) with the formal banking system for savings and credit.

• It is one of the largest microfinance programmes in the world and a major tool for financial inclusion and women's empowerment.

NOTE

• A Self Help Group (SHG) is a small voluntary group (usually 10–20 members, often women) who pool savings and provide small loans to members.

question: In which among the following years was Hindu widow remarriage declared legal in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1856.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Hindu widow remarriage was legalised in 1856 through the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856. The Act was passed largely due to the efforts of the social reformer Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar. (हिंदू विधवा पुनर्विवाह अधिनियम — 1856)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Act was passed during the governor-generalship of Lord Canning (Lord Dalhousie initiated it).

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a great educationist and reformer of Bengal who also worked for women's education.

NOTE

• Other reform legislation: Abolition of Sati (1829, Lord Bentinck), Age of Consent Act (1891), Child Marriage Restraint (Sarda) Act (1929).

question: Annapurna Devi is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Surbahar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Annapurna Devi was a renowned Hindustani classical musician associated with the Surbahar (a bass sitar). She belonged to the Maihar gharana and was a disciple/daughter of Ustad Allauddin Khan. (सुरबहार — अन्नपूर्णा देवी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Surbahar is a plucked string instrument similar to the sitar but larger, producing a deeper, bass sound.

• Annapurna Devi was awarded the Padma Bhushan; she was known for her reclusive life and dedication to teaching.

NOTE

• Instrument–artist pairs: Sitar (Ravi Shankar), Sarod (Amjad Ali Khan), Flute (Hariprasad Chaurasia), Sarangi (Ram Narayan), Santoor (Shivkumar Sharma).

question: Who regarded Vedas as the source of all knowledge and known for the slogan 'Go back to the Vedas'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swami Dayanada Saraswati.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Swami Dayananda Saraswati, the founder of the Arya Samaj (1875), regarded the Vedas as the source of all true knowledge and gave the famous slogan "Go Back to the Vedas". (वेदों की ओर लौटो — स्वामी दयानंद सरस्वती)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• He wrote "Satyarth Prakash" (The Light of Truth) and opposed idol worship, casteism, child marriage and superstitions.

• The Arya Samaj promoted women's education, widow remarriage and the Shuddhi movement; it founded DAV (Dayanand Anglo-Vedic) institutions.

NOTE

• Other reformers: Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Brahmo Samaj, 1828), Swami Vivekananda (Ramakrishna Mission, 1897), Keshab Chandra Sen (Brahmo Samaj leader).

question: Rigveda is the earliest specimen of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indo European language.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rigveda is the earliest specimen (oldest surviving text) of the Indo-European language family. It is composed in Vedic Sanskrit, which belongs to the Indo-Aryan branch of the Indo-European languages. (ऋग्वेद — इंडो-यूरोपीय भाषा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas (Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda) and is a collection of hymns (suktas) dedicated to various deities.

• The Indo-European language family includes Sanskrit, Latin, Greek, Persian, and most European languages.

NOTE

• The Gayatri Mantra is from the Rigveda. The Rigveda's 10th Mandala contains the Purushasukta, which mentions the four varnas.

question: What is the length of the men's kabaddi court?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13 m.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The standard men's kabaddi court measures 13 metres in length and 10 metres in width. (पुरुष कबड्डी कोर्ट — 13 मीटर लंबाई)

• For women (and juniors), the court is slightly smaller — 12 m × 8 m.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kabaddi is a traditional Indian contact team sport; a "raider" enters the opponents' half chanting "kabaddi" and tries to tag defenders and return.

• India has dominated the Kabaddi World Cup and the sport is popular through the Pro Kabaddi League (PKL).

NOTE

• Court dimensions for SSC: Kabaddi (men) 13 m × 10 m, Hockey 91.4 m × 55 m, Cricket pitch 22 yards (20.12 m).

question: Which of the given options is rod-shaped, carries genetic information, is visible only at cell division and is present in the nucleus?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chromosomes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chromosomes" are rod-shaped (thread-like) structures present in the nucleus that carry the genetic information (DNA/genes) and become clearly visible only during cell division. (गुणसूत्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Humans have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs) in each body cell, including one pair of sex chromosomes (XX in females, XY in males).

• A chromosome is made of DNA and proteins (histones); a segment of DNA that codes for a trait is called a gene.

NOTE

• Lysosomes are "suicidal bags"; ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis; cytoplasm is the jelly-like fluid of the cell. Only chromosomes carry hereditary information.

question: Prerana Shrimali received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in which of the following years for her contribution to the Kathak dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2009.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Prerana Shrimali, a distinguished Kathak dancer, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2009 for her contribution to the dance form. (प्रेरणा श्रीमाली — कथक — 2009)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Prerana Shrimali is associated with the Jaipur gharana of Kathak and was a disciple of Kundan Lal Gangani.

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, established in 1952, is India's national academy for music, dance and drama.

NOTE

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dances, mainly of North India, known for fast footwork (tatkar), spins (chakkars) and abhinaya. Its main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

question: Which gas is released when you combine vinegar and baking soda in a balloon, causing it to inflate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carbon dioxide.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When vinegar (acetic acid) reacts with baking soda (sodium bicarbonate), it releases carbon dioxide (CO₂) gas, which inflates the balloon. (कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड)

◦ Reaction: NaHCO₃ + CH₃COOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂↑

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• This is a classic acid–base (neutralisation) reaction that produces a salt, water and carbon dioxide gas.

• The same principle (release of CO₂) is used by baking soda/baking powder to make cakes and bread rise.

NOTE

• CO₂ turns lime water milky and does not support combustion (it is used in fire extinguishers). It is also released during respiration and fermentation.

question: From 13 September 2023, DMK MP Tiruchi Siva has been appointed the chairperson of the Committee on __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Industry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• From 13 September 2023, DMK MP Tiruchi Siva was appointed the Chairperson of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry. (उद्योग संबंधी समिति — तिरुचि शिवा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Parliamentary Standing Committees examine bills, budgets and policies in detail and assist Parliament in its oversight function.

• They are broadly of two types: Standing Committees (permanent) and Ad hoc Committees (temporary).

NOTE

• The Department-Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) were introduced in 1993; they help in the detailed scrutiny of the demands for grants and bills of various ministries.

question:
Which of the following Rights is mentioned in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution?

A) Right to Freedom: Protection of life and personal liberty  B) Right against Exploitation: Prohibition of trafficking in human beings and forced labour  C) Right to Equality: Equality before law  D) Right to Freedom of Religion: Freedom to manage religious affairs
option_1: Right to Freedom: Protection of life and personal liberty
option_2: Right against Exploitation: Prohibition of trafficking in human beings and forced labour
option_3: Right to Equality: Equality before law
option_4: Right to Freedom of Religion: Freedom to manage religious affairs
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to Freedom: Protection of life and personal liberty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 21 of the Constitution guarantees the "Protection of Life and Personal Liberty" — no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. It is part of the Right to Freedom (Articles 19–22). (अनुच्छेद 21 — प्राण एवं दैहिक स्वतंत्रता का संरक्षण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Over time, Article 21 has been widely interpreted by the Supreme Court to include the right to a dignified life, livelihood, privacy, clean environment, education (Article 21A) and more.

• Along with Article 20, Article 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency (44th Amendment).

NOTE

• The other options wrongly match the articles: Article 14 (Equality before law), Article 23 (against trafficking/forced labour), Article 26 (manage religious affairs).

question: The Sahitya Akademi award winning novel 'Zindaginama' was written by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Krishna Sobti.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hindi novel "Zindaginama" was written by Krishna Sobti, for which she received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1980. (ज़िंदगीनामा — कृष्णा सोबती)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Krishna Sobti is a celebrated Hindi writer; she was also awarded the Jnanpith Award (2017), India's highest literary honour.

• Her other notable works include "Mitro Marjani", "Dil-o-Danish" and "Ai Ladki".

NOTE

• Amrita Pritam (Punjabi writer — "Pinjar"), Mahadevi Verma (a poet of the Chhayavaad movement) and Mannu Bhandari ("Aapka Bunty") are other major Hindi/Punjabi literary figures.

question: Who among the following is worshipped as Nataraja before many classical dance performances in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shiva.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lord Shiva, in his form as "Nataraja" (the "King/Lord of Dance"), is worshipped before many classical dance performances in India. Nataraja represents Shiva performing the cosmic dance (Tandava). (नटराज — भगवान शिव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Nataraja form shows Shiva dancing within a ring of flames, symbolising the cosmic cycle of creation and destruction.

• The famous Nataraja temple is at Chidambaram (Tamil Nadu).

NOTE

• The Tandava is the vigorous, masculine dance of Shiva; the Lasya is the gentle, graceful dance associated with Parvati. Nataraja bronzes are masterpieces of Chola art.

question: The famous 'Tripartite struggle' for supremacy occurred between which of the following powers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gurjar-Pratihara, Rashtrakuta and Palas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous "Tripartite Struggle" (8th–9th centuries CE) was fought among three powerful dynasties — the Gurjara-Pratiharas, the Rashtrakutas and the Palas — for control over the city of Kannauj (Kanyakubja), which was a symbol of sovereignty over North India. (त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष — कन्नौज हेतु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kannauj was strategically important and prestigious; whoever controlled it was seen as the paramount power of North India.

• The Gurjara-Pratiharas ultimately gained control of Kannauj for a long period.

NOTE

• Key rulers: Gurjara-Pratihara (Nagabhata I, Mihira Bhoja), Rashtrakuta (Dhruva, Govinda III), Pala (Dharmapala, Devapala). The struggle weakened all three, aiding later invasions.

question: Four resistors of equal resistance R each are connected in various possible ways both in series and/or parallel to get different combined resistances. Which of the following values of resistance cannot be achieved by using all the four resistors?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 R.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Using all four equal resistors (R each), the value "2 R" cannot be obtained in any valid series/parallel combination, whereas the others can:

◦ 0.25 R = all four in parallel (R/4 = 0.25 R).

◦ 1.33 R = one resistor in series with three resistors in parallel (R + R/3 = 4R/3 ≈ 1.33 R).

◦ 2.5 R = two in series (2R) + two in parallel (R/2) → 2R + 0.5R = 2.5 R.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Series: R_total = R₁ + R₂ + ... (resistances add up).

• Parallel: 1/R_total = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + ... (for equal resistors in parallel, R_total = R/n).

NOTE

• In series, the total resistance is more than the largest; in parallel, it is less than the smallest. Combining series and parallel gives intermediate values.

question: The remains of Great Bath have been found from the excavation at which of the following Harappan sites?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohenjodaro.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous "Great Bath" — a large, watertight tank used possibly for ritual bathing — was found at the Harappan site of Mohenjo-daro (in present-day Sindh, Pakistan). (महान स्नानागार — मोहनजोदड़ो)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Great Bath is one of the earliest public water tanks; it was made watertight using bitumen (natural tar) and finely fitted bricks.

• Mohenjo-daro ("Mound of the Dead") was excavated by R. D. Banerji (1922) and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• Site–feature pairs: Great Bath & Great Granary (Mohenjo-daro), Dockyard (Lothal), Ploughed field & fire altars (Kalibangan), Rows of granaries (Harappa).

question: As per HDI 2021, which of the following neighbouring countries of India had the highest female life expectancy at birth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maldives.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Human Development Index (HDI) 2021, among the given neighbouring countries of India, the Maldives had the highest female life expectancy at birth. (एचडीआई 2021 — मालदीव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The HDI, published by the UNDP (United Nations Development Programme), measures development using three dimensions — health (life expectancy), education (years of schooling) and standard of living (GNI per capita).

• The HDI was developed by economists Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen.

NOTE

• Life expectancy at birth is the average number of years a newborn is expected to live. It is a key indicator of the health and living conditions of a country.

question: What is the retirement age of Judges serving at the Supreme Court of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 65 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A Judge of the Supreme Court of India holds office until he/she attains the age of 65 years (retirement age). (उच्चतम न्यायालय के न्यायाधीश — 65 वर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• A High Court Judge retires at the age of 62 years.

• Supreme Court Judges are appointed by the President (Article 124); they can be removed only through impeachment for proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

NOTE

• The Supreme Court is the apex court of India (Article 124). The sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court is the Chief Justice + up to 33 other judges (34 in total).

question: According to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 2022-23, which state of India is the largest producer of sugarcane?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (2022-23), Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of sugarcane in India. (उत्तर प्रदेश — गन्ना का सबसे बड़ा उत्पादक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Uttar Pradesh is followed by Maharashtra and Karnataka in sugarcane production.

• Sugarcane is a Kharif cash crop that needs a hot and humid climate; India is the second-largest producer of sugarcane in the world (after Brazil).

NOTE

• The sugar industry is the second-largest agro-based industry in India (after textiles). Sugarcane is the raw material for sugar, jaggery (gur), khandsari and ethanol.

question: Which of the following peaks is NOT located in the Himalayan mountains?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalsubai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kalsubai" is NOT a Himalayan peak — it is the highest peak in Maharashtra, located in the Western Ghats (Sahyadri range). (कलसुबाई — पश्चिमी घाट, हिमालय में नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Nanda Devi (Uttarakhand) and Kamet (Uttarakhand) are high peaks of the Himalayas.

• Annapurna is a Himalayan massif in Nepal.

NOTE

• Highest peaks by region: Kanchenjunga (highest in India, Himalayas), Anamudi (highest in South India, Western Ghats), Kalsubai (highest in Maharashtra), Doddabetta (Nilgiris).

question: Chithirai festival of Tamil Nadu is dedicated to which of the following Goddesses?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meenakshi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Chithirai festival" of Tamil Nadu, celebrated grandly at Madurai, is dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi. It marks the celestial wedding of Goddess Meenakshi with Lord Sundareswarar (Shiva). (चिथिराई महोत्सव — देवी मीनाक्षी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The festival is held at the famous Meenakshi Amman Temple in Madurai and is one of the largest festivals of Tamil Nadu.

• It usually takes place in the Tamil month of Chithirai (April–May).

NOTE

• The Meenakshi Temple at Madurai is a masterpiece of Dravidian architecture, known for its towering, colourful gopurams (gateway towers).

question: India won its first Olympic gold in hockey in which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1928.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India won its first Olympic gold medal in hockey at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics. This marked the beginning of India's golden era in hockey. (1928 एम्स्टर्डम ओलंपिक — भारत का पहला हॉकी स्वर्ण)

• The legendary Major Dhyan Chand was a star of that team.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India won six consecutive Olympic hockey gold medals from 1928 to 1956 (1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956).

• In all, India has won 8 Olympic gold medals in hockey.

NOTE

• Major Dhyan Chand is called the "Wizard/Magician of Hockey"; his birthday (29 August) is celebrated as National Sports Day.

question: The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted in which year by the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2013.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted in 2013. It aims to provide subsidised foodgrains to about two-thirds of India's population (up to 75% of rural and 50% of urban population). (राष्ट्रीय खाद्य सुरक्षा अधिनियम — 2013)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Under the NFSA, eligible beneficiaries get foodgrains (rice, wheat, coarse grains) at highly subsidised prices through the Public Distribution System (PDS).

• It also has special provisions for pregnant women, lactating mothers and children (nutritional support), giving a legal "Right to Food".

NOTE

• The Act covers two categories: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households (poorest) and Priority Households (PHH).

question: Gabbro is an example of which type of rocks?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Igneous rock.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gabbro" is an example of an igneous rock. It is a coarse-grained, intrusive (plutonic) igneous rock formed by the slow cooling and solidification of magma deep beneath the Earth's surface. (गैब्रो — आग्नेय चट्टान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Igneous rocks are formed by the cooling of magma/lava. They are of two types: intrusive/plutonic (cooled below the surface, e.g., granite, gabbro) and extrusive/volcanic (cooled on the surface, e.g., basalt).

• Igneous rocks are also called "primary rocks".

NOTE

• The three rock types: Igneous (from magma/lava), Sedimentary (from deposited sediments, e.g., sandstone, limestone) and Metamorphic (formed by heat/pressure, e.g., marble, slate).
